claims.text: Eutectic high-entropy alloy design can achieve concurrent improvement in strength and ductility.
Computational optimization of material properties enables the concurrent strength–ductility improvement.
The proposed starting material is a cast eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The intervention computationally designs and optimizes alloy composition and microstructure.
Processing parameters are optimized to form a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Computational design and process optimization produce a refined microstructure.
The resulting microstructure has an optimized phase distribution and grain size.
Optimized alloy composition and microstructure simultaneously enhance strength and ductility.
Optimized alloy composition and microstructure reduce the traditional trade-off between strength and ductility.
The designed alloy will exhibit a 20% increase in yield strength relative to traditional alloys.
The designed alloy will exhibit a 30% increase in elongation at break relative to traditional alloys.
The comparison baseline is conventional high-entropy alloys that have not undergone computational design optimization.
The proposed approach is outside its stated applicability boundary when compositions or processing conditions produce non-eutectic microstructures.
The magnitude of strength–ductility improvement may depend on the specific alloy system and processing conditions.
